page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton2 processors built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. Operating on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, the instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with single-threaded execution per core. It is configured with 64 GB of system memory, yielding an extensive memory-to-core ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 64 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache, along with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography.

Storage and networking capabilities include a bundled 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate average uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 67.02 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 32.5 GB/sec, matching its memory-centric architecture. However, raw compute metrics show noticeable constraints: Geekbench 6 single-core (931.0) and multi-core (3104.0) scores, along with PassMark CPU benchmarks, rank within the bottom tiers, reflecting the moderate clock speed and architectural limits of first-generation Neoverse-N1 compute under heavy calculation loads.

By delivering high memory capacity per core without the cost of high vCPU counts, the instance provides strong resource efficiency for memory-bound applications. The inclusion of fast local NVMe storage complements workloads that require transient caching or low-latency swap space. Amazon Web Services x2gd.xlarge is suitable for in-memory databases like Redis, caching layers, real-time analytics engines, and memory-intensive containerized services that do not demand extensive mathematical processing or high single-thread CPU performance.
description: Amazon Web Services x2gd.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 4-core AWS Graviton2 ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It offers 64 GB of memory, delivering a 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside a 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance store and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate solid uncached memory throughput reaching 67.02 GB/sec read and 32.5 GB/sec write, whereas compute-focused metrics such as Geekbench and PassMark reflect lower relative processing power. The instance provides a cost-efficient hardware profile for environments that require vast memory capacity and fast scratch storage without paying for unnecessary vCPUs. It is best suited for in-memory data stores, caching layers, and database workloads requiring high RAM-to-core allocations.
